subject: System Design
title: What Is Consensus
description: A quick, practical guide to What Is Consensus.

hook.text: Five servers need to agree on who the leader is. Two think it's server A, three think it's server B. Chaos.

buildup.text: Consensus is the process of getting multiple nodes to agree on a single value, even when some fail.

discovery.text: Consensus algorithms ensure safety: nodes never disagree, and progress: they eventually decide.

twist.text: The FLP impossibility theorem proves that consensus is impossible with even one faulty node in an async system.

climax.text: Practical algorithms like Raft and Paxos use timeouts to work around FLP and achieve consensus in practice.

punchline.text: Getting distributed nodes to agree is harder than it sounds.

quiz.question: What is consensus in distributed systems?
options: Getting multiple nodes to agree on a single value
